title: SSW Kaigo
subtitle: Nursing care Japanese for Specified Skilled Worker (介護)

units.title: Dignity and independence
units.intro: Care in Japan starts from the person, not the task. Respect the user's choices, support what they can still do themselves, and protect their privacy.

terms.note: Every care action should protect the person's dignity.
Help only where needed so the person keeps using their own abilities.
The user decides; the carer explains and offers choices.
Care planned around one person's life, habits and wishes.
In principle not allowed; only in strict emergencies with team decisions and records.

questions.q: A user can button her own shirt, but slowly. What fits 自立支援 (support for independence)?
options: Wait and let her do it, helping only with the hard buttons
Button it for her to save time
Tell her to wear clothes without buttons from now on
Ask another user to help her
questions.why: Supporting independence means letting the person use the abilities they still have.

questions.q: A user says he does not want to bathe today. What respects 自己決定?
options: Listen to his reason and offer another time or a body wipe
Take him to the bath anyway because it is the schedule
questions.why: Respect the choice, find out why, and offer alternatives.

questions.q: Which is an example of 身体拘束 (physical restraint)?
options: Tying a user to a wheelchair so they cannot stand up
Helping a user walk with a cane
Opening the curtains in the morning
questions.why: Restricting someone's movement with ties, rails or locks is restraint.

questions.q: You are helping a user change clothes in a shared room. What protects プライバシー?
options: Close the curtain and cover the body with a towel
Keep the door open so staff can see
Change clothes quickly in the hallway
Ask other users to look away
questions.why: Curtains and towels protect privacy and dignity.

units.title: Communication
units.intro: Good care needs good talk: listen fully, speak before you touch, and use polite, clear Japanese.

terms.en: speaking to the person (before and during care)
terms.note: Tell the person what you will do before you do it.

terms.jp: 非言語コミュニケーション
terms.reading: ひげんごコミュニケーション
terms.note: Face, eye level, tone, gestures, touch.

terms.en: small listening responses (like はい, そうですね)

terms.note: Useful for users with hearing loss.

questions.q: Before helping a user stand up, what should you do first?
options: Say what you are going to do (声かけ) and wait for a response
Lift the user quickly before they get nervous
Stand behind the user without speaking
Ask a colleague to explain later
questions.why: 声かけ lets the user prepare and agree.

questions.q: A user with dementia repeats the same story. Which response shows 傾聴?
options: Listen, nod and respond as if hearing it for the first time
questions.why: Active listening accepts the person's feelings even when the story repeats.

questions.q: A user hears very little. Which method can help?
options: 筆談 (writing on paper or a board)
questions.why: Writing, facing the person and speaking slowly all help.

questions.q: Which is good 非言語コミュニケーション when talking to a user in a wheelchair?
options: Crouch to the user's eye level and smile
Stand tall and look down at the user
Look at your phone while talking
questions.why: Eye level and a calm face make the user feel respected.

units.title: Body and mind
units.intro: Ageing, illness and dementia change what each person needs. Know the common conditions so you can notice changes early.

terms.en: affected side (the weak or paralysed side)
aspiration (food or drink going into the airway)

questions.q: A user who stays in bed all day gets a red spot on the hip that does not fade. What may be starting?
questions.why: Pressure on one spot for a long time causes pressure ulcers; change position regularly.

questions.q: Older people often feel less thirsty. Which risk does this raise?
questions.why: Offer drinks often, even when the user says they are not thirsty.

questions.q: A user has paralysis on the right side. Which side is the 健側?
questions.why: 健側 is the unaffected side; here, the left.

questions.q: A user coughs and chokes while drinking tea. What could have happened?
options: 誤嚥: some tea went into the airway
脱水: the user is too hydrated
questions.why: Coughing while drinking can be a sign of aspiration; watch the posture and report it.

units.title: Moving and transfers
units.intro: Transfers are where falls happen. Use good body mechanics, check the brakes, and work with the user's own strength.

terms.en: sitting on the edge of the bed

questions.q: Before a 移乗 from bed to wheelchair, what must you check?
options: The wheelchair is as far from the bed as possible
The footrests are down so the user can stand on them
The user is still lying down
questions.why: Brakes on and footrests up prevent the chair from moving and the user from tripping.

questions.q: When helping a user who walks with a cane in the right hand, where do you usually stand?
options: Slightly behind on the user's weak (affected) side
On the cane side, holding the cane
Far away so the user feels independent
questions.why: You support the side where the user is more likely to fall.

questions.q: What does 体位変換 help prevent?
questions.why: Changing position relieves pressure on the skin.

questions.q: Which is good body mechanics for the carer?
options: Keep the user close, bend your knees, and use your legs
Keep your legs straight and bend your back
Lift with your arms stretched out far
questions.why: A wide base, bent knees and staying close protect your back.

units.title: Eating and oral care
units.intro: Safe eating depends on posture, pace and texture. Clean mouths help prevent pneumonia.

terms.en: to choke and cough (on food or drink)

questions.q: Which posture is safer for eating?
options: Sitting up with the chin slightly down
questions.why: Sitting upright with the chin a little down makes swallowing safer.

questions.q: Why add とろみ to tea for some users?
options: Thick drinks move slower and are less likely to go into the airway
questions.why: Thickened drinks lower the risk of aspiration for users with swallowing problems.

questions.q: Why is 口腔ケア important for older people?
questions.why: Bacteria in the mouth can cause pneumonia if aspirated.

questions.q: During 食事介助, how should you give food?
options: Small spoonfuls, checking the user has swallowed before the next
questions.why: Small amounts at the user's pace are safest.

units.title: Bathing and dressing
units.intro: Bathing relaxes and cleans, but carries risks: temperature shock, falls and fatigue. Dressing follows a simple rule for a weak side.

terms.en: undress the healthy side first, dress the affected side first

questions.q: A user's left arm is paralysed. Following 脱健着患, which sleeve do you put on first?
questions.why: Dress the affected side first; undress the healthy side first.

questions.q: Before the user gets into the bath, what should you check?
options: The water temperature with your own hand or a thermometer
Only the colour of the water
questions.why: Always check 湯温 to prevent burns.

questions.q: How can you reduce the risk of ヒートショック in winter?
options: Warm the changing room and bathroom beforehand
Bathe right after a big meal
questions.why: Small temperature differences between rooms lower the strain on the body.

questions.q: A user feels unwell and cannot bathe today. What can you offer instead?
options: 清拭 (wiping the body with warm towels)
Skip all cleaning for a week
questions.why: A bed bath keeps the skin clean without the strain of bathing.

units.title: Toileting
units.intro: Toileting is private and emotional. Protect the user's feelings, keep their routine, and watch for changes.

questions.q: A user still feels 尿意 and can sit. What is better than using おむつ all the time?
options: Help the user use the toilet or a portable toilet
Limit their drinks so they urinate less
Change the diaper only once a day
questions.why: Using the toilet keeps independence and dignity.

questions.q: How do you respect 羞恥心 during 排泄介助?
options: Close the door or curtain and wait outside if it is safe
Watch the whole time and comment
Talk loudly about it with other staff
questions.why: Privacy reduces embarrassment.

questions.q: A user has had no bowel movement for several days. What might this be, and what do you do?
options: 便秘; record it and report to the nurse or leader
questions.why: Record and report changes; carers do not decide medication alone.

questions.q: A user had an accident (失禁) and looks upset. What do you say?
options: Calmly say you will help them change and keep it private
Scold them so it does not happen again
Tell everyone in the dining room
questions.why: Stay calm and protect the user's feelings.

units.title: Safety, infection and records
units.intro: Prevent infections with standard precautions, report near misses, and write facts so the next shift knows what happened.

terms.reading: ひょうじゅんよぼうさく

terms.en: near miss (an incident that almost caused harm)

questions.q: Under 標準予防策, when should you wear gloves?
options: When you may touch blood, body fluids, or excretions
questions.why: Standard precautions treat all body fluids as possibly infectious.

questions.q: A user almost slipped in the hallway but you caught them. What should you do?
options: Report it as a ヒヤリハット so the team can prevent it next time
Say nothing because nobody was hurt
questions.why: Near-miss reports help prevent real accidents.

questions.q: Which is a good 記録?
options: “14:20 Coughed while drinking tea; stopped and sat upright; no fever.”
questions.why: Records should be factual, timed and specific.

questions.q: When is 手洗い needed?
options: Before and after care for each user
Only at the start of the shift
questions.why: Washing before and after each care stops infections spreading between users.
